key_insight: Deep learning models plus high-throughput functional assays enable large-scale discovery and de novo design of internal ribosome entry sites (IRES), allowing programmable control of cap‑independent translation in mRNA.
problem_solved: The field lacked scalable, predictive methods to find and engineer functional IRES elements for tunable translation, slowing design of RNA therapeutics and synthetic gene circuits.
method: Massively parallel functional screens (high‑throughput reporter assays) to measure IRES activity across thousands of sequences.
Train predictive deep learning models that map RNA sequence (and inferred structure) to translation efficiency.
Use generative/design algorithms and an iterative design–test loop to propose and experimentally validate de novo IRES sequences with desired activity.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners this provides a real-world sequence→function benchmark and a demonstration of closed‑loop model‑guided biological design, highlighting opportunities for generative models, uncertainty-aware optimization, and transfer learning in molecular engineering.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: screening → model training → generative design → experimental validation (iterative loop).
Bar or violin plot comparing translation activity of natural, screened, and de novo IRES variants.
Sequence logo / motif map and secondary-structure schematic showing features the model learned to exploit.
Heatmap or scatter plot of predicted vs. measured activity to illustrate model accuracy and design gain.
paper_title: Programmable RNA translation through deep learning-driven IRES discovery and de novo generation
paper_authors: Yanyi Chu, Di Yin, Dan Yu, Guangxue Xu, Junze Zhang
